themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: This week, Tottenville/Great Kills residents filed 22 complaints about dead or dying trees—a 329% spike from the 5.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling either accelerated tree decline or a sudden awareness event; this aligns with the community board's repeated multi-year budget requests for forestry services and street tree maintenance.
evidence: 22 dead/dying tree complaints this week vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (329% spike, z-score 5.59)
Overgrown Tree/Branches complaints also spiked 277% two weeks ago (25 complaints vs 6.6 avg), suggesting broader tree maintenance failure
Community board has requested forestry services and street tree maintenance funding for multiple consecutive years, indicating chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Investigate whether weather, disease, or deferred maintenance is driving the spike; interview Parks Department about tree health in district
Profile residents dealing with hazardous dead branches over homes and streets; examine why forestry budget requests have gone unfunded

themes_detail.label: Flooring/Stairs Structural Failures
themes_detail.summary: This week, the district saw 5 complaints about flooring and stair failures—a 344% surge from a 1.1 weekly baseline—suggesting a sudden wave of building code violations or aging housing stock deterioration that could pose immediate safety risks to residents.
evidence: 5 flooring/stair complaints this week vs. 1.1 weekly average (344% spike, z-score 6.46)
No prior spike pattern in 8-week baseline, indicating this is a NEW issue, not seasonal
742 building permits filed in last 90 days (366 alterations, 33 demolitions), suggesting active but potentially unvetted construction activity
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for DOB violation details on these 5 complaints; determine if they cluster in specific buildings or neighborhoods
Interview residents on failing stairs/flooring; investigate whether landlords are ignoring maintenance during renovation boom

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Last week, the district logged 4 noise-related park complaints, a 3100% spike from a 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score 11.72)—the highest-severity statistical anomaly in the dataset—suggesting either a sudden change in park usage patterns, new activity (concerts, events, youth gatherings), or a coordinated community response to a specific disturbance.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike, z-score 11.72, highest severity in dataset)
Spike is isolated to ONE week; not a sustained trend, suggesting acute event or viral complaint campaign
No Reddit discussion or local news coverage detected, indicating story may not have broken into mainstream media yet
reporting_angles: Identify which park(s) generated the complaints; visit sites to observe current conditions and talk to neighbors about what changed
Contact Parks Department and NYPD to determine if there was a specific event, gathering, or enforcement action last week

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Missed Collections Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Two weeks ago, the district reported 53 missed garbage collection complaints—a 312% surge from the 12.9 weekly average—indicating either a service disruption, staffing shortage, or route failure that may have since resolved or persists; this aligns with the community board's repeated demands for increased illegal dumping enforcement.
evidence: 53 missed collection complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 12.9 weekly average (312% spike, z-score 3.76)
Community board has requested increased illegal dumping law enforcement funding for multiple consecutive years
Peak spike occurred 2 weeks ago; no current-week data provided to confirm whether issue persists
reporting_angles: Check with Sanitation Department on whether there was a documented service disruption 2 weeks ago and current status
Canvass residents to determine if collections have resumed or if complaints have simply plateaued

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Disappearances
themes_detail.summary: Last week, residents reported 6 missing street signs—a 433% spike from the 1.1 weekly baseline—indicating either vandalism, storm damage, or deferred maintenance that could create navigation and safety hazards, particularly for delivery services and emergency responders.
evidence: 6 missing street sign complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 3.36)
Isolated to one week; pattern unclear without more context
DOT has received repeated community board budget requests for street reconstruction, suggesting infrastructure maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Map which intersections are missing signs; determine if there's a geographic cluster suggesting targeted vandalism or weather damage
Contact DOT on sign replacement timeline and whether this spike correlates with recent storms or construction
